To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce a low-fidelity video encoder optimization method to jointly optimize a video encoder and a temporal action localization head.

(i) a video encoder trained on a source domain is sub-optimal for TAL, (ii) a joint video encoder and TAl head training can resolve the sub-optimality, and (iii) a low-fidelity training method enables joint optimization to be feasible under the same memory constraints.

1) a low-fidelity optimization of the video encoder can significantly boost the performance of existing temporal action localization methods, and 2) the performance can be further enhanced by jointly optimizing the video and TAL heads.
